podcast.title: Tribute Concept for Shangri-La Dee Da (1980)
podcast.body: Andrew Wood, from the Seattle band Mother Love Bone, died of an overdose in 1980. Stone Temple Pilots' "Shangri-La Dee Da" album was originally intended as a double album, partly as a tribute to Wood, complete with a documentary film and a coffee table book, though the concept was scaled back by the record company. "This record was supposed to be a double album, something about it being a tribute to Andrew Wood of the Seattle band Mother Love Bone, who died of an overdose back in 1980."

podcast.title: Overdose Death
podcast.body: Andrew Wood, the lead singer of the acclaimed Seattle band Mother Love Bone, tragically died from an overdose. His passing led to the band's hiatus and inspired the formation of the tribute project, Temple of the Dog. "the overdose death of their lead singer Andrew Wood."

xref.title: Andrew Wood's Death and STP Tribute Idea (1980)
xref.body: Andrew Wood, a member of the Seattle-based band Mother Love Bone, died of an overdose in 1980. Stone Temple Pilots had planned to dedicate their "Shangri-La Dee Da" album as a double-album tribute to him, though this elaborate concept was ultimately rejected by their record label. "This record was supposed to be a double album, something about it being a tribute to Andrew Wood of the Seattle band Mother Love Bone, who died of an overdose back in 1980."

xref.title: Andrew Wood's Death (March 19, 1990) – Heroin Overdose
xref.body: Andrew Wood, the popular singer of Mother Love Bone, died on Monday, March 19, 1990, the day before their album *Apple* was due for release. He was found comatose on March 16 after a heroin overdose, and after brain activity ceased, his family chose to take him off life support. "Andrew was a really popular guy, and he had lots of friends in Seattle. His death hit Chris Cornell, his old roommate particularly hard."

xref.title: Frontman's Tragic Death (1990)
xref.body: Mother Love Bone, a band described as local heroes "poised for big things," had their dreams shattered when their frontman, Andrew Wood, died of a heroin overdose. His death occurred just days before their major label album was scheduled to be released, cutting short their potential rise. "Mother Lovevone, some local heroes that were poised for big things had their dreams shot to hell when frontman Andrew Wood died of a heroin overdose just days before their major label album was supposed to come out."

xref.title: Performance with Chester Bennington (2008)
xref.body: During the 2008 Project Revolution Tour, Chris Cornell was performing when Chester Bennington unexpectedly joined him on stage to sing "Hunger Strike." This Temple of the Dog song was written by Cornell as a tribute to his late roommate, Andrew Wood of Mother Lovevont. "If we go back to the 2008 project revolution tour, Chris was on the bill. And when he stepped forward to sing the Temple of Dog Song, Hunger Strike, a song written for and dedicated to Chris's late roommate Andrew Wood of Mother Lovevont, Chester surprised everybody by coming in to sing with him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Andrew Wood Memorial
xref.body: Temple of the Dog was a Seattle supergroup formed specifically to record an album in memory of Andrew Wood, the singer of Mother Love Bone, who died of a heroin overdose. The project brought together surviving members of Mother Love Bone and friends from Soundgarden. "Some of the surviving members of Mother Love Bone got together with friends from Soundgarden, a few other local musicians to record an album in Andrew's memory. They called their Seattle group Temple of the Dog."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Andrew Wood's Cause of Death
xref.body: The official cause of Andrew Wood's death was hypoxic encephalopathy, a condition resulting from his brain being deprived of oxygen due to him ceasing to breathe when he fell into his comatose state, causing irreversible damage. "The official cause of death was hypoxic encephalopathy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Andrew Wood's Death
xref.body: Lead singer Andrew Wood overdosed on heroin, suffered a massive cerebral hemorrhage, and died just before the release of their debut album, "Apple." His death was a crucial event that set in motion the formation of other bands and projects like Temple of the Dog, contributing to the scene's coalescence. "Not just before that album was released, their singer Andrew Wood, overdosed on heroin, suffered a massive cerebral hemorrhage, and died."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Andrew Wood's Death Precedes Album Release
xref.body: Andrew Wood died only a few days before Mother Love Bone's album, "Apple," was scheduled for release. "Only a few days before the Mother Love Bone album was supposed to be released."

xref.title: Andrew Wood's Death and Life Support Removal
xref.body: Three days after being found comatose, doctors advised that there was no hope for Andrew Wood's recovery, and life support was removed. He died at 3:15 pm on Monday, March 19, 1990. "Life support was removed, and Andrew died at 3.15 pm on Monday, March 19, 1990."

xref.title: Andrew Wood's Drug Overdose and Coma
xref.body: On March 16, 1990, Andrew Wood was discovered comatose by his girlfriend after he had injected himself with heroin, leading to his hospitalization and placement on life support. "On March 16, 1990, Andrew was found comatose by his girlfriend after he'd shot himself up with heroin."

xref.title: Andrew Wood's Early Drug Use
xref.body: Andrew Wood began smoking pot at the age of 11, and transitioned to harder drugs in his late teens, leading to multiple unsuccessful attempts at rehabilitation. "He was a pot smoker at 11. Hard drugs came along in his late teens."

xref.title: Andrew Wood's Roommate at Time of Death
xref.body: Chris Cornell was Andrew Wood's roommate at the time of his death, a detail that ties into the formation of Temple of the Dog as a tribute. "Andrew's roommate at the time he died was Chris Cornell."

xref.title: Band Disintegration after Singer's Death
xref.body: Mother Love Bone dissolved after their singer, Andrew Wood, died from a heroin overdose. This event led Stone Gossard and Jeff Ament to seek new musical projects, eventually leading to the formation of what would become Pearl Jam. "Stone and Jeff were looking for something to do after their band Mother Love Bone fell apart when their singer Andrew Wood died of a heroin overdose."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation as a Tribute
xref.body: Temple of the Dog was formed as a one-time-only band specifically as a tribute to Andrew Wood, who was Chris Cornell's roommate and a member of Mother Love Bone. "And as a tribute, he formed a one-time only band called Temple of the Dog."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Impact of Andrew Wood's Death
xref.body: The formation of Temple of the Dog and subsequently Pearl Jam raises questions about whether these collaborations would have occurred had it not been for Andrew Wood's untimely death. "So it makes you wonder if they would have ever come together, but not been for Andrew's death."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Legacy and Band Spin-offs
xref.body: Following Andrew Wood's death, the surviving members, bassist Jeff Ament and guitarist Stone Gossard, along with friends from Soundgarden, formed Temple of the Dog to record a memorial album. The positive experience of these sessions eventually led Ament and Gossard to form Pearl Jam. "Some of the surviving members of Mother Love Bone got together with friends from Soundgarden, a few other local musicians to record an album in Andrew's memory."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Roommate of Andrew Wood – Impact on Temple of the Dog
xref.body: Chris Cornell shared an apartment with Andrew Wood, the singer of Mother Love Bone. Wood's unexpected death in March 1990 profoundly affected Cornell, leading him to write songs in tribute that eventually formed the basis of the Temple of the Dog project. "Andrew died the day Chris got back from a long tour with Soundgarden. A few days after the funeral, Chris and Soundgarden headed out on a European tour, and while on the road, Chris started running some songs in tribute to his old friend."

xref.title: Transformation into Pearl Jam – Post-Tragedy Rebirth
xref.body: Following the tragic death of Andrew Wood, the surviving members of Mother Love Bone, Jeff Ament and Stone Gossard, collaborated with Chris Cornell and Matt Cameron to form Temple of the Dog. This collaboration eventually led Ament and Gossard to form a new band with Eddie Vedder, initially called Mookie Blaylock, which soon became Pearl Jam. "When Mother Lovebone collapsed and turned into Pearl Jam, Kelly became their full-time manager, leaving Susan to deal with Allison Chains."

xref.title: Tribute to Andrew Wood
xref.body: Temple of the Dog was formed as a quick tribute to Andrew Wood, Chris Cornell's former roommate and the singer of Mother Love Bone, who tragically died in March 1990. Cornell wrote several songs in his friend's honor, which he then shared with the surviving members of Mother Love Bone, leading to the formation of this supergroup. "When he got back to Seattle, he showed the surviving members of Mother Love Bone, the songs. When other materials started flowing, they decided to record a quick tribute album under the name Temple of the Dog."
